commit.message:
Viewer: replay a seed read-only, or drive an interactive cluster

Two modes instead of flags that blurred them. A seed replays exactly
the run the headless simulator does for it, faults and all, and nothing
can be injected, since that would make it a different run: the fault
keys are inert and the legend says so. --interactive builds a perfect
cluster with no seed, three replicas unless told otherwise, requests
that never run out, one tick of latency so messages can be seen, and
short heartbeat and timeout, where nothing goes wrong until a fault is
injected. On quit it prints the injected faults as a script, which
--script replays on the same cluster.

-By default nothing goes wrong unless you make it: the network is reliable
-and only the faults you inject happen, at one tick per second. `--chaos`
-uses the seed's random faults like the headless simulator, and `--until`
-runs at full speed to a tick and pauses there, for stepping into a failure
-a seed reproduces. On quit it prints the seed and every fault you injected
-as a script, and `--script FILE` replays one, so a scenario found by hand
-becomes a reproducible run.
+`--interactive` is a perfect cluster with no seed: nothing goes wrong until
+you inject a fault, at one tick per second. On quit it prints every fault
+you injected as a script, and `--script FILE` replays one, so a scenario
+found by hand becomes a reproducible run. A seed instead replays the run
+the headless simulator does for it, faults and all, and is read-only;
+`--until` runs at full speed to a tick and pauses there, for stepping into
+the failure a seed reproduces.
